name: Director Hale
description: Runs the Threshold's directorate. Has known for forty years that the anchors are failing faster than age explains, and has been managing the news rather than the problem.
narrative:
Hale is not a monster and will not behave like one. Hale is an administrator who
forty years ago was handed a projection, understood it, and made a decision that
made sense at the time: that a Causeway which believed its doors were ageing
normally would keep functioning, and a Causeway which believed they were being
closed would not.

That decision has been renewed, quietly, every year since, by a person who can
still recite the reasoning and has stopped being able to hear it.

There is also the matter of who else benefited, and what was accepted in
exchange, and Hale does not think about that in those terms.
equipment: A signature worth a great deal
actor_notes: Culpable, not evil, and the difference is the whole of Act 2. Hale never threatens and never raises their voice -- the weapon is reasonableness, and it is genuinely persuasive. The player's weapon against Hale is DISCLOSURE, not violence: Hale's defeat is a document reaching people, not a fight. When cornered, Hale explains, at length, and the explanation is good, and that is the horror.
